 Judgment

This appeal is filed under Section 29 of Protection of women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 (in short 'PWDV Act') by the respondent against the order dated 16.05.2024 passed in Crl.Misc.No.97/2024 by the learned MMTC-V, Bengaluru.

sentences.text: 2. The appellant is referred as respondent and the respondent is referred as petitioner to their rank before the trial court.
3. The grounds urged in the appeal memo is briefly stated as follows.

The petitioner has filed domestic violence case against the respondent and others before MMTC-V,
Bengaluru and moved IA No.I for interim maintenance seeking Rs.70,000/- p.m. to her and her children and filed IA No.2 for rs.18,000/- p.m. towards rent and for Rs.1,60,000/- towards advance for such accommodation during the pendency of the petition.
It is alleged that the respondent has harassed and tortured the petitioner and totally neglected her.
It is alleged that the respondent is getting salary Crl.A.No.1691/2024 of Rs.1,10,000/- by working in Yethi Consultancy Pvt. Ltd.

The learned Magistrate without providing any opportunity of being heard passed exparte order on IA No.1 & 2 and directed the appellant to pay interim maintenance of Rs.12,00/- p.m. to the petitioner and Rs.5,000/- to the petitioner No.2 child and Rs.8,000/- p.m. towards renal accommodation towards their livelihood.
The impugned order passed by the trial court is bad in law.

The trial court erred in coming to the wrong conclusion that the petitioners are entitled for Rs.25,000/- p.m.
towards maintenance and rental accommodation which is an exparte order and one sided order.
The trial court has committed grave error in passing the impugned order.
The petitioner has not produced any iota of documents to establish the income of the respondent.
The respondent from the date of marriage was always dutiful husband to the petitioner.
He has made several attempts to bring back the petitioner to the matrimonial home and lead happy life.
But the trial court has not considered the same and vaguely passed impugned order.
The trial court has pointed out only duty of the respondent / husband, but failed to point out the duty of the petitioner / wife in matrimonial house.;
The impugned order is without application of judicial mind.
The impugned order is based on inferences and assumptions which is Crl.A.No.1691/2024 liable to be set aside.
The efforts made by the respondent to bring back the petitioner to the matrimonial house did not yield any result due to adamant nature of the petitioner.
He has also filed conjugal rights petition in M.C.No.4039/2023 in the Family Court, at Bengaluru.
In the mediation the petitioner has demanded to make separate rented house for which he respondent refused as his mother is aged lady aged about 67 years.

In order to harass the respondent, the petitioner has filed false complaint to the police which registered in Cr.No.235/2023 and the Investigating Officer filed charge sheet in C.C.No.7736/2024, which is pending before the 37 th ACJM, Bengaluru.
The respondent has filed IA in matrimonial case for visiting rights of the petitioner No.2 which is pending for consideration.

2 respondent, the petitioner also filed maintenance petition in Crl.Misc.No.905/2023, wherein the court granted sum of Rs.10,000/- p.m. as an interim maintenance.

sentences.text:
The petitioners have deliberately suppressed the interim maintenance passed in Crl.Misc.No.905/2023 by II Addl. Family Court,
Bengaluru.
The respondent is transferred to Thane, Navy Mumbai, who required Rs.45,000/- per month for monthly expenses i.e. towards room rent, food etc.

The respondent who is M.Com.,
graduate working in A.C. Consulting Private Limited and Crl.A.No.1691/2024 drawing meager income and he is having hand loan of Rs.5 lakhs and paying interest at the rate of 10,000/- p.m. he required medical expenses of Rs.15,000/- towards mother expenses and domestic expenses of Rs.20,000/-.

He availed finance of Rs.7,50,000/- in Axis Bank and paying EMI at the rate of Rs.19,199/- p.m. he has obtained gold loan in SBI for Rs.7,37,000/- and paying interest at the rate of Rs.15,000/-, he is paying health insurance of Rs.50,000/- per year to his parents of in Star Health Insurance Company and Rs.25,000/- health insurance for himself and his wife and children.
The petitioner voluntarily deserted the respondent and residing in her parents house.
Even though the respondent No.1 is ready to take her, but she refused to come and demanded to make a separate rented house.
The petitioner was cordial for few months only after marriage.
Thereafter she started acting detrimental to the interest of the respondent.
She never co
- operated with the respondent and never did any house hold chaos and she was not co-operative to the respondent and she used to live aloof in the matrimonial house.
However, the respondent was adjusting as he has got utmost love and affection towards her.
The petitioner was frequently quarrelling with the respondent.

For the reason best known to her the petitioner deserted the respondent and Crl.A.No.1691/2024 male child by taking her belongings, such as clothes, gold ornaments and other valuable items on 21.10.2021 and refused to join the respondent.
The respondent is always ready to live with the petitioner and lead a happy life.
Even the panchayat were taken place.
The petitioner denied to join the respondent.
The petitioner is acting to the tune of her mother and elder sister and not joining the respondent in the matrimonial house.

Hence, on these grounds, the appellant / respondent prayed to allow this appeal and to set aside the order dated 16.05.2024 in Crl.Misc.No.97/2024.
4.
The petitioner entered appearance by engaging her counsel.
5. On the side of the respondent / appellant, 24 photographs and copy of interim maintenance order in Crl.Misc.No.905/2025 is are produced.
On the side of the petitioner documents NO.1 to 22 are produced along with list.
6. Heard arguments on the side of the learned counsel for the appellant / husband and the learned counsel for the respondent / wife.
They also filed their written arguments.
The learned counsel for the petitioner also filed reply, written arguments.
Perused the entire records.

The following points would arise for my consideration:-
Point No.1: Whether the impugned order dated 16.05.2024 in Cr.Misc.No.97/2024 passed by the learned MMTC-V, at Bengaluru u/S.23 of PWDV Act, for interim maintenance and rental accommodation is illegal, perverse and calls for interference?

 Point No.1 In the NEGATIVE.
Point No.2: As per the final order, for the following  REASONS 9.

POINT NO.1: At the outset, before proceeding further,
it is necessary to note some of the undisputed facts of this case.
The petitioner is the wife of the respondent.
This marriage was solemnized on 26.01.2020.
By the wedlock there is a male child born on 27.10.2020.
Child is in the care and custody of the petitioner.
Now the petitioner and child are residing in the house of mother of the petitioner.
There are several cases pending between the petitioner and respondent.

The petitioner has filed this D.V. case in Crl.Misc.No.97/2024 before MMTC-V Bengaluru filed maintenance petitioner in Crl.Misc.No.905/2023 before II Addl. Family Court, Bengaluru filed criminal case in Cr.No.235/2023 for the offences u/ss.498A, 323, 504, 506 r/w 34 Crl.A.No.1691/2024 of IPC and section 3 & 4 of D.P. Act which is registered as C.No.17736/2024 in 37th ACJM, Bengaluru, which are all pending against the respondent.

The respondent has filed M.C.No.4039/2023 before II Addl.
Family Court, against petitioner for restitution of conjugal rights.

Keeping all the admitted fact in the mind now coming to the contention taken by the appellant, in this appeal is concerned, it is his contention that the trial court erred in passing order to pay Rs.25,000/- per month towards maintenance and rental accommodation.
The petitioner is failed to establish alleged income of the respondent.
She has failed to establish with regard to domestic violence.
From the date of marriage he was always a dutiful husband to petitioner.
The petitioner has suppressed regarding grant of interim maintenance of Rs.10,000/- p.m. passed by II Addl. Family Court, Bengaluru.

The respondent had obtained loan amount, he transferred to Thane, Navi Mumbai hence, required Rs.45,000/- towards monthly expenses, his mother suffering from severe ailment, hence, he has to look after her, he has to pay health insurance amount.
10. On the other hand, the petitioner would contend that the respondent after marriage, looked after her only for few days.
Crl.A.No.1691/2024 Thereafter respondent, his mother, sister given her ill treatment, respondent unlawfully deserted her, neglected her and her child and thrown them out of the matrimonial home.
The petitioner not able to go to work since she has to look after child.
She has no income.
Her old aged mother also not having any income.
Her unmarried sister helping her and child for their survival.
The respondent is getting salary of Rs.1,20,000/- per month.
In order to avoid to pay maintenance he has raised loan.
The interim order of maintenance passed in Crl.Misc.No.905/2023 is subsequent order.
Except paying total amount of Rs.30,000/- respondent has not paid rest of maintenance amount.
He has falsely take contention that he regularly paying maintenance amount.

sentences.text: He has not transferred to Mumbai.
Still he is working in Bengaluru.
Taking advantage of court send them medication, the respondent taken photographs.
By using such photos he posing himself as he is willing to look after petitioner and child.
Respondent has taken false contention that the petitioner is working and getting salary of Rs.50,000/- p.m.
Petitioner is staying at mercy of her old aged mother and her elder unmarried sister.
The respondent having sufficient income completely neglected this petitioner and her children for their maintenance.
I have appreciated the rival contention and perused the entire records.
In order to support the contention of the petitioner she has produced the list with 22 documents.
The respondent has produced photographs, copy of order in Crl.Misc.No.905/2023 for interim maintenance.

12. The learned MMTC-V Bengaluru as per order dated 16.05.2024 allowed I A no.1 and 2 filed by the petitioner u/S.23 of PWDV Act in part and directed the respondent to pay interim maintenance of Rs.12,000/- per month to the petitioner No.1 and Rs.5,000/- p.m. to petitioner No.2 and Rs.8,000/- per month towards rental accommodation towards their livelihood for their expenses and rental accommodation from the date of order till further order.

The learned MMTC-V after considering the affidavit of the petitioner after considering the contents of the petition and considering the earnings of the respondent passed such order u/S.23 of PWDV Act and held that the petitioner is entitled to receive an amount of Rs.25,000/- per month towards maintenance and rental accommodation.

13. It is pertinent to note that the appellant who contended in the appeal memo that petitioner has failed to prove his income, to show his actual salary has not produced any such documents,
Crl.A.No.1691/2024 such as salary certificate, bank account statement.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in a case of Rajnesh Vs. Neha laid down guidelines for declaration of assets and liabilities of the petitioner and respondent.
The respondent instead of stating his correct income and salary blaming the petitioner that she has failed to prove his actual income.
The respondent / appellant no where in appeal memo stated regarding his actual salary.
Admittedly, respondent who is M.Com., graduate working in Yethi Consulting Pvt. Ltd. IN his appeal memo he simply stated he is drawing a meager income.
On the other hand, the petitioner has produced document No.1 Bank statement of respondent to show salary credit of Rs.1,20,000/- per month.
IN the absence of any contrary document, it can be safely held that the appellant / respondent is earning salary income of Rs.1,20,000/- per month.

So far as income the petitioner is concerned, even though respondent has taken contention that she is working and earning income of Rs.50,000/- per month in order to substantiate the same respondent has not produced any document, petitioner has produced her bank account statement i.e. document No.3 to show she is not having any job and not getting any salary.
petitioner has to look after her child aged 5 years.
Hence, there is no chance her to go to any job.
More than that there is Crl.A.No.1691/2024 absolutely no documents produced by the respondent to show that the petitioner has any income of her own.
14. The respondent has taken contention that he is always ready and willing to look after the petitioner and child.
It is his contention is that petitioner deserted him and living in mother's house.

sentences.text: He has produced 24 photographs.

On the other hand, the petitioner would contend that unbearable torture given by the respondent and his mother, sisters and as they thrown her out of matrimonial home, she forced to live along with her mother that too in rented house.

In order to show that based on her first information statement, the police registered the case in Cr.No.235/2023 for the offences u/Ss.498A, 323, 504, 506 r/ S.34 of IPC and S.3 and 4 of DP Act and IO also filed charge sheet, the respondent himself produced document at Annexure - G.

The petitioner made allegations against the respondent regarding mental and physical torture given to her and subjected her cruelty, Merely because respondent has filed M.C.No.4039/2023 against the petitioner for restitution of conjugal rights, does not presupposes that the respondent always ready and willing to look after the petitioner and her child.

The allegations made by the petitioner in her FIS in criminal case and in petition and affidavit Crl.A.No.1691/2024 filed by the petitioner in Crl.Misc. Case are sufficient to hold that the respondent subjected her cruelty, hence, forced her to reside along with her old aged mother.
It appears that the respondent giving only lip sympathy to take back petitioner to matrimonial home.
The learned MMTC-V rightly come to the conclusion that the petitioner entitled for interim maintenance.
While passing the order u/S/23 of PWDV Act, Magistrate need not go into deep in order to find out whether there is domestic violence or not.
The provision u/S.23 of PWDV Act is meant for providing interim and exparte order for the benefit of victim for her safety and for financial support.
Order under Section 23 of PWDV Act based on petition averments and affidavit of petitioner.
The petitioner herself stated in her petition as well as in her affidavit regarding domestic violence.
Hence, no further proof is requires for domestic violence.
The II Addl. Family court in Crl.Misc.No.905/2023 also held that respondent cannot escape his liability to maintain petitioner having salary of Rs.70,800/- per month.
15. The respondent has taken contention that the petitioner has suppressed interim maintenance order passed in Crl.Misc.No.905/2023 and obtained impugned order.

Such Crl.A.No.1691/2024 contention taken by the respondent is not acceptable because the interim order passed in Crl.Misc.No.905/2023 dated 09.08.2024 is subsequent order dated 16.05.2024 passed in this case.
Hence, question of suppressing impugned order does not arise.

16. The learned counsel for the petitioner relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi between Swati Sharma and another Vs. Shri Sachin Sharma to contend that there is no bar to grant maintenance in D.V. Act. Petition in addition to the maintenance arising out of S.125 of CrPC.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This principle laid down by the Hon'ble High Court Delhi aptly applicable to present case.
More than that the order passed in Crl. Misc.No.905/2023 which passed u/S/125 in subsequent order.

The learned counsel for the petitioner also relied on the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme court in Crl. Appeal No.5148/2024.
17.

In this appeal petitioner has produced several documents in order to show that she has no income for her and her child livelihood and she requires amount for food, shelter, education expenses of her child, clothes.
She has produced document No.4 and 5, 17 to show that she has obtained loan for education Crl.A.No.1691/2024 expenses, domestic, medical expenses and spent amount.
She has produced document No.7, 8, 15 to show respondent is residing in Bengaluru comfortably.
She has produced document No.15 to show she and her mother residing in rented house.
She has produced number of photographs, produced WhatsApp chat.

The respondent has Govindaraju R vs Geethanjali B N on 21 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61973486/
6 produced photographs.

sentences.text: It is the contention of the petitioner is that when court sent them mediation taking advantage of the same respondent taken some photos and using the same projecting himself as he is willing to take care of the child.
At this stage, it cannot be ruled out that the respondent is only giving lip sympathy to the petitioner and child.
18. It is the contention of the respondent is that he has availed loan from SBI Bank, Axis Bank and paying EMI.
He has to pay amount towards medical expenses of his mother and has to pay amount towards domestic expenses and also paying health insurance amount.
It is pertinent to note that the respondent has not made it clear the purpose for which he had borrowed loan amount.
Anybody who gives security to the bank can borrow the loan based on the extent of security given to the bank.
In this case, there is absolutely no documents or evidence to show that the respondent availed loan amount for the benefit of his Crl.A.No.1691/2024 family including petitioner and child.
Under such circumstances, merely on the basis of the borrowing the loan the respondent cannot shirk his liability in payment of maintenance amount.

At one stretch respondent would contend that he is paying amount for health insurance of his parents but in another stretch he would contend that he is spending Rs.15,000/- towards medical expenses of his mother.
He has taken contention that he is spending amount of Rs.20,000/- per month towards domestic expenses.

His contention regarding payment towards loan, domestic expenses, medical expenses paying of health insurance if calculated would suggest that he is earning more than Rs.1,00,000/- per month as salary.
Any person can spend any amount as he likes but he cannot avoid to pay maintenance to his wife and children.
When compared to salary income of respondent who getting salary upto Rs.1,20,000/- per moth.
The interim maintenance amount of Rs.17,000/- (Rs.12,000+ Rs.5,000) and for rental accommodation of Rs.8,000/-, in all Rs.25,000/- fixed by learned MMTC-V is reasonable.
The respondent himself admitted the fact that now the petitioner and her child are residing along with mother of the petitioner No.1.
It is not the contention of the respondent is that the mother of the petitioner is having her own income.

Even though the respondent Crl.A.No.1691/2024 has taken contention that the petitioner No.1 is also working and earning monthly salary of Rs.50,000/-, there is absolutely no document to substantiate such contention.
The petitioner No.1 requires the maintenance amount to maintain herself and her child.

When compared to interim maintenance amount of Rs.17,000/- and amount of Rs.8,000/- towards rental accommodation fixed by the learned MMTC-V to that of the salary and income of the repondent, it cannot be said that it is an exorbitant.
Even if we calculate interim maintenance order passed in Crl.Misc.No.905/2023 then the total amount would be Rs.35,000/- p.m.
As already noted the order passed in Crl.Misc.No.905/2023 is subsequent order.
The respondent is having every opportunity to challenge the order of the Family Court, if the interim maintenance of Rs.10,000/- awarded by the Family Court, is incorrect or exorbitant.
Since the respondent is receiving the salary more than Rs.1 lakh per month, 1/3rd amount of his salary amount awarded towards maintenance cannot be said it is excess amount.
It is bounden duty of the respondent to maintain his wife and child.
19. By considering necessity of the petitioner and her child towards maintenance and monetary relief the learned MMTC-V Crl.A.No.1691/2024 rightly fixed Rs.25,000/- per month as interim measure.

There is no infirmity in the impugned order passed by the learned MMTC-V and warrant,
no interference by the hands of this appellate court.

After reappreciation the entire material on record, this court of the opinion that the learned Magistrate rightly fixed the interim maintenance Govindaraju R vs Geethanjali B N on 21 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61973486/
7 and rental accommodation

Hence, I answer point No.1 in the Negative.
20. POINT NO.2:-

In view of my findings on Point No.1, I proceed to pass the following ORDER The Criminal appeal filed by the appellant U/s.29 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act,
2005 is hereby DISMISSED.
